title: The Alibi of Saint Alder's
premise: Mara Sterling, the meticulous archivist of Saint Alder's Cathedral, has spent fifteen years keeping the cathedral's secrets—and her own—safely filed away. When twin letters arrive, one confessing to the unsolved death of choirboy Thomas Wren and one promising 'the rest of the truth' before the anniversary dinner, Mara realizes the case everyone declared closed was buried alive, and she may be its only living witness. As she digs through the locked crypt's records, she uncovers a conspiracy among the cathedral's founding families to protect one of their own, and discovers that her own found family—the verger, the organist, the cook—each hold a fragment of that night. The killer is Father Ambrose Hale, now the beloved dean, who silenced Thomas after the boy witnessed a theft of restoration funds; in the climax, Mara traps him into confession during the anniversary toast using the second letter's promised evidence hidden in the crypt, and chooses to expose him at the cost of the only home she has ever had.
about_author: Juniper Sandoval is a former parish records clerk from the coastal town of Greyhaven who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of church ledgers before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet people who keep dangerous archives.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Establishes Saint Alder's, Mara's obsessive filing system, and her pride in never taking an unclosable case. She notices the crypt seal has been disturbed—fresh wax over an old lock. Emotional beat: controlled contentment shadowed by unease; something in her ordered world has already shifted.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Two letters arrive unsigned: one confessing to Thomas Wren's death fifteen years ago, one promising 'the rest of the truth before the toast is raised.' Mara recognizes the handwriting as half-familiar. Emotional beat: dread curdling into professional resolve—she takes the case.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with flashback texture. She pulls the official record: ruled accidental drowning, case closed by unanimous agreement of the vestry. Interviews the gentle verger Odell, who flinches at Thomas's name. Emotional beat: the first crack in her belief that closed cases stay closed.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Dean Ambrose Hale announces the cathedral's 150th-anniversary dinner, to be held in three weeks—a deadline matching the letters. Mara watches Hale work the room, beloved and untouchable. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; the clock is now public.

chapters.title: What the Organist Remembers
chapters.summary: Organist Sef's POV. Sef recalls the night Thomas died—the choir practice that ended early, a voice arguing in the cloister, and Hale's car leaving late. He has told no one for fifteen years out of loyalty. Emotional beat: guilt as a slow poison; found family beginning to fracture under questioning.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the archive she finds gaps in the restoration fund records from exactly the year Thomas died—money siphoned during the crypt renovation. Someone with archive access altered the books. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the crime was financial first, fatal second.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A third letter appears inside her own locked desk: 'You were there too, Mara.' A fragment of memory surfaces—rain, a small hand, running. Emotional beat: vertigo; the investigator realizes she is evidence.

chapters.title: Cook's Confession, Partial
chapters.summary: Cook Ilsa's POV. Ilsa admits she saw young Mara near the crypt that night and said nothing, believing she was protecting the child. She warns Mara that some of the old families will bury this again. Emotional beat: tenderness laced with fear; the found family's complicity revealed.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She maps the vestry of fifteen years ago: four names, three still attending Saint Alder's, all donors to the restoration fund. One, Edith Vane, agrees to talk—if Mara comes alone. Emotional beat: stepping off safe ground into open danger.

chapters.title: Edith's Bargain
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith reveals the theft was real and that Hale covered it up when Thomas threatened to tell, but claims she has no proof—and that proof was sealed in the crypt. She asks Mara to let it stay buried. Emotional beat: temptation of comfortable silence offered plainly.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Mara and Odell's alternating POV. They open the crypt legally, citing an inventory audit. Inside: Thomas's effects, misfiled as 'relic fragments,' including a notebook. Emotional beat: reverent dread; the dead boy finally speaks through paper.

chapters.title: Thomas's Notebook
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The notebook documents the missing funds and names the thief—but the final pages are water-blurred, the name half-legible. It could be Hale. It could be someone else. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into obsession.

chapters.title: Someone Searches Her Rooms
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her cottage is turned over; the notebook's hiding place known only to her and Odell is empty. She suspects a leak within her found family. Emotional beat: betrayal; trust becomes a liability she can't afford but can't abandon.

chapters.title: Odell Breaks
chapters.summary: Odell's POV. Odell confesses he moved the notebook—not to steal it, but because fifteen years ago he helped carry Thomas's body to the water, believing it an accident, and has been paying for it ever since. Emotional beat: grief and forgiveness entangled; the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: The Memory Returns
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, dreamlike. Full memory floods back: nine-year-old Mara hid in the crypt during a storm, saw the argument, saw Thomas fall—struck, not drowned—and ran when Hale's eyes swept the dark. He knew she was there. He has always known. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Hale Invites Her to Tea
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Hale, courteous and chilling, speaks in parables about archives, forgetting, and mercy. He offers her a promotion and a quiet life if the notebook is 're-shelved.' Emotional beat: the seduction of erasure, refused.

chapters.title: Sef's Recording
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef reveals he kept a cassette from fifteen years ago—a rehearsal tape that caught the argument in the cloister, Hale's voice unmistakable. He was afraid to listen for fifteen years. Emotional beat: courage passed like a candle between friends.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Dinner
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She assembles the chain: ledger gaps, notebook, tape, Edith's testimony, her own memory. Hale attempts to burn the archive wing's older stacks; Mara and Odell save the Wren file from the flames. Emotional beat: siege mentality; the family closes ranks around the truth.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, high tension. At the anniversary dinner, as glasses rise, Mara stands and reads Thomas's final notebook page aloud, then plays the tape. Hale, composed, calls it forgery—until Mara produces the second letter's promised evidence: his own original confession, written years ago and sealed in the crypt by his younger, guilt-ridden hand. Emotional beat: cathartic detonation.

chapters.title: Confession in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Hale's POV, brief and hollow. Confronted below the cathedral, Hale admits everything—the theft, the blow, the drowning staged, the years of good works as penance he never believed in. Police take him through the cloister where Thomas died. Emotional beat: the banality of a monster unmasked.

chapters.title: Reopening the Case
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The coroner reclassifies Thomas's death; the Wren family, distant and scattered, receives the notebook. Mara formally amends the archive: the case, at last, closed correctly. Emotional beat: exhausted peace; the record is true even if nothing else is restored.

chapters.title: What the Cathedral Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. Weeks later, Mara catalogs the crypt honestly for the first time, leaves flowers on Thomas's shelf, and shares supper with Odell, Sef, and Ilsa—her found family, scarred but intact. She writes one final letter, unsigned, and files it. Emotional beat: quiet grace; memory honored, survival paid for, belonging earned.
